title: Inclusionary zoning deferred amid market uncertainty
subtitle: Beaver Creek Road funding, road program changes, Wood Lily Park design, online parking permits and fire plan consulting.
overview: Council voted to defer inclusionary zoning in the city's protected major transit station areas {{vote:m12}}. Staff will bring a zoning by-law to the March 24, 2025 meeting that delays the start date to an undetermined time, and will report back in June 2025 with a proposed new date. The reason given was uncertainty over provincial and federal policy and possible US tariffs. Without action, the rules would have taken effect on March 31, 2025.

Council also released partial funding for the Beaver Creek Road and Conservation Drive reconstruction, a major project for new development in the northwest of the city, and directed staff to tender the road and underground work. It adjusted the road reconstruction program, deferring Amos Avenue and adding Shakespeare Place and Shakespeare Drive and Moore Avenue for 2026.

Council approved the Wood Lily Park concept design, funding for an online parking permit and paid parking system, a consultant for Fire Master Plan work, and a new truck-mounted sewer cleaner. It supported a liquor licence for a local brewery.

decisions.detail: Council directed staff to bring a by-law to the March 24, 2025 meeting deferring inclusionary zoning to an undetermined date, with a report in June 2025 proposing a new implementation date {{vote:m12}}.

decisions.item: Beaver Creek Road and Conservation Drive
decisions.detail: Council released partial capital funding of $30,300,000 for the road and underground work, mostly from development charge debentures, and directed staff to tender it, while pumping station tendering waits for a further report.

Council deferred Amos Avenue, added Shakespeare Place and Shakespeare Drive for 2026, advanced Moore Avenue for 2026, redistributed the funding, and directed staff to finalize a cost-sharing agreement with Kitchener.
Council approved the preferred concept, released $528,000 in 2025 capital funding, and directed staff to proceed with detailed design.
Council approved $50,000 in each of 2025 and 2026 from the Parking Reserve Fund for an online permit and hourly parking system, with ongoing costs to be considered in the 2027 budget.
Council awarded the consulting contract for implementing Fire Master Plan recommendations to John MacDonald Architect for a total of $642,944.10.
Council awarded the supply of a truck-mounted combination sewer cleaner to Joe Johnson Equipment Inc. for a total of $828,492.

debate: Staff recommended a pause on inclusionary zoning, citing a weakened market: high construction costs and interest rates, a large supply of unsold condos, and uncertainty over tariffs. They noted the rules depend on a healthy market and that Kitchener had paused its program too.

A developer who spoke said little is being built and that a decision tonight would change little, but that the added cost of affordable units would slow any recovery. Costs would be spread across the market units, which are already priced too high.

One councillor proposed proceeding now with exemptions for projects with site plans in by March 31 and a two-year window to pull permits. The aim was to give the development industry certainty and fairness. That motion was replaced by the mayor's amendment.

The mayor argued for waiting on provincial and federal decisions and tariffs, and said inclusionary zoning is one tool among others such as the 2025 University Avenue project. Two councillors opposed deferral, saying delay keeps pushing back help for people at risk of losing housing.

On Beaver Creek Road, one councillor noted the project depends heavily on development charge debt and urged senior governments to contribute. On Amos Avenue, a councillor asked when it would return and was told it will be reassessed with other roads.
